episode_in_one_sentence: AI moves out of the chat box into background work, playful creations, personal archives, small-business tools, and reproducible scientific tasks.

listener_notes.note: Imagine followed by OpenAI just shipped that made a hypothetical completed job sound like a reported outcome.
Six matched builds and a three-three split were concrete; the final hardware tease overlapped Social.
Another model race repeated Marcus's experiment, and visual-use examples lacked explicit hypothetical framing.
The archive and chess stories were strong, but the desk became a rapid catalogue of extra finds.
Local design and family fables had promise; the long tail of skills and repositories diluted them.
Four launches became eight; the usable-today claim was not supported for every product.
The lamp, doorbell, and timer sounded like reported devices; swimming in the koi pond was unsupported.
Dots functionality and Muse connectors were explained for a second time.
Reproduced references and fixed grading made CompMat-Bench a strong lab pick.
The close repeated three desk experiments and then added a fourth try.

after_evidence.hook: The 83-word opening names Dots in the first sentence and asks what the listener would delegate; about 32 seconds at 155 words per minute.
after_evidence.audience_fit: Seven desks each own three substantive stories. Personal archives, chess, games, family fables, consumer travel, audio creation, and DIY hardware outweigh enterprise-platform coverage.
after_evidence.inspiration: Every substantive story ends in a proposed use, and the close offers a birthday fable, an event audio welcome, and a book-oriented e-reader concept.
after_evidence.science_value: Research leads with computational-materials autonomy. The named Share this with your lab beat follows science.json's exact lab_pick, takes about 69 seconds, and explains reproduced references and fixed-rule grading. YouTube carries the scientific video and Builders carries Openclatura.
after_evidence.caution_budget: The only safety and evidence-limitation discussion follows Now, the reality check in Research. It contains three items and takes about 57 seconds. Fiction labels elsewhere distinguish hypothetical ideas from reports, not safety advice.
after_evidence.specificity: The script preserves the 53-minute keynote, more than 20 launches, six matched builds, three-three result, four game-playing models, six autonomy levels, and 94-task benchmark. Sources do not name the Mac utility, so no product name was invented.
after_evidence.non_redundancy: The community and launch catalogues are gone. Dots has one substantive capability explanation; Social uses the Verge's audience-question angle only. Model release economics, coding-build comparison, and creative outputs have distinct owners.
after_evidence.clarity_for_ear: Lint finds zero sentences over 30 words and a 10.2-word average. First, Next, Finally, and Now mark story changes. Some explicit hypothetical labels remain to meet the factual-framing requirement.
after_evidence.momentum: A named stage launch starts the show; the coding tie, chess adaptation, family fable, combined voice-and-music product, koi pond, and lab benchmark provide fresh turns every desk. Desks run about 2.4–3.5 minutes.
after_evidence.voice_distinctness: Marcus uses Okay so and a stage-to-demo lens; Priya jokes that her calendar is a model menu; Sam likes a scrappy chess adaptation; Maya explains tool structure; Diego frames products by buyer; Lena pictures creative outputs; Aaron connects scientific vocabulary to inspectable work.
after_evidence.flow_and_handoffs: All seven correspondents return to Jordan with different complete handback lines containing back to you. Marcus picks up the anchor before the main story, Priya's cue callbacks the keynote, and the other cues pivot briefly without summarising.
after_evidence.accuracy: The red-door query and lamp/timer ideas are explicitly hypothetical. Unsupported koi swimming, blanket immediate availability, weekend-build promise, and twenty-minute lab outcome are removed. Added or changed factual content is mapped to allowed JSON item IDs and URLs in the change log.
after_evidence.tts_readiness: Model versions are spoken as five point five and six point one. Software development kits and language-model-based agents replace ambiguous acronyms; only familiar AI, GPT, and API remain. No symbols or break tags.
after_evidence.close: Exactly three concrete, explicitly proposed projects are followed by three opportunity questions about Dots jobs, Muse devices, and longer scientific workflows. The sign-off names the AI Brief Hub without a URL.

warnings_left_by_design.reason: Sonnet five point five is a necessary spoken product name in four genuinely distinct contexts: coding comparison, release economics, creative showcase, and the reality check. The idea to steal is the requested recurring action beat, used three times with different actions. Neither repeats a story or an experiment.

The flagged tokens are common connective language and the mandatory factual-framing words imagine and reported: another, imagine, familiar, rather, reported, something, format, finished, conversation, borrow. Manual story-ownership and action checks find no repeated substantive advice. Replacing imagine merely to satisfy token counting would weaken the explicit hypothetical framing.

This is informational, not a lint warning. AI, GPT, and API are familiar letter-spoken tokens permitted by the skill. SDK, LLM, PDF, ESP32, and WebMCP are removed or written out where their stories remain.

timing_detail.method: 155 spoken words per minute plus music for the lint estimate; top-level duration additionally includes configured post-silence.

summary_for_producer: The draft had a strong opportunity-first premise and lab pick, but invented illustrations sounded reported, several desks became catalogues, and handbacks repeated. The edit keeps all seven desks, gives each three substantive stories, labels hypothetical uses clearly, and preserves CompMat-Bench as the named lab beat. All cautions remain in Aaron's roughly 57-second reality check; the episode runs about 21.3 minutes before minor configured pauses. Next week, keep single story ownership and check illustrative examples before they reach the script. No audio was rendered and no git command was run.
